name: Saltmarsh Telecom
employees: 203,000 direct; 80,000 contracted tower and node technicians
sovereign_territory: Saltmarsh Signal Zones — not a contiguous territory but a patchwork of 4,400 sovereign signal towers, 900 buried fiber nodes, and twelve orbital relay licenses covering the entire GLMZ corridor and extending into the surrounding rural collapse zones. Administrative headquarters: the Saltmarsh Spire, a 340-meter communications tower and office complex in former Cleveland.
founding_story: Saltmarsh emerged in 2135 from the wreckage of three collapsed municipal telecom utilities after the Great Signal Blackout — a cascading infrastructure failure that left 40 million Meridian residents without communications for eleven days. The blackout's architect was never officially identified, but Saltmarsh's first CEO, a former signals intelligence officer named Daria Holt, built the entire network on the assumption that it would be attacked again. Every node is hardened, redundant, and capable of autonomous operation. Holt's paranoia became Saltmarsh's brand: 'The signal that doesn't die.'
security_force: Saltmarsh Signal Guard (SSG) — 19,000 personnel, heavily specialized in electronic warfare and counter-intrusion. Every SSG unit carries a personal signal-hardening suite and is trained to maintain communications infrastructure under active cyberattack. Their most feared capability is the DEADBAND protocol — a localized signal blackout weapon that can silence all non-Saltmarsh communications in a 40-kilometer radius, used twice in corporate conflicts and once, controversially, during a Meridian labor uprising in 2161.
key_detail: Saltmarsh holds sovereign licensing rights to the 6.8 GHz band across the entire Meridian corridor — a spectrum allocation locked in during the post-blackout emergency charters of 2135 that no subsequent legal challenge has successfully overturned. This means every corponation, government remnant, and private citizen in Meridian is, at some level, a Saltmarsh tenant.
relationship_to_big_20: Ranked #13. Vantablack Media is their largest content-transmission client and also their most adversarial contract partner — renegotiating aggressively every three years. Cinderblock AI requires Saltmarsh signal infrastructure for all external cognitive leasing. Kelpline Logistics' VINE AI communicates exclusively over Saltmarsh encrypted backbone.
full_text: SALTMARSH TELECOMMUNICATIONS & SIGNAL SOVEREIGNTY CORP. — Stock: SMTC-88 — Sector: Telecommunications & Signal Infrastructure. Valuation Φ1.7 trillion. Revenue Φ290 billion annually. 203,000 direct employees; 80,000 contracted technicians. Sovereign territory: 4,400 signal towers, 900 buried fiber nodes, twelve orbital relay licenses, and the Saltmarsh Spire headquarters in former Cleveland. Founded 2135 by Daria Holt in the aftermath of the Great Signal Blackout, which silenced 40 million residents for eleven days. Holt built every node to survive attack — a founding paranoia that became the company's core identity. Security arm, the Signal Guard, fields 19,000 electronic warfare specialists and holds the DEADBAND protocol: a 40-kilometer localized signal blackout weapon deployed twice in corporate conflicts and once during a labor uprising. Core legal advantage: sovereign licensing rights to the 6.8 GHz band across all of Meridian, locked in during post-blackout emergency charters and never successfully challenged. Every entity in the corridor is a Saltmarsh tenant at some level. Ranked #13 in the Big 20. Primary signal infrastructure for Cinderblock AI's external leasing operations. Largest and most combative content-transmission client: Vantablack Media.

glmzTerritory.description: Waukegan lakefront relay hub plus 4,400 sovereign signal zones distributed throughout the GLMZ. Controls approximately 67% of data traffic north of Zone 2. Primary headquarters at the Waukegan lakefront complex; relay architecture threads through every zone in the Corridor.
glmzTerritory.grayZoneRelationship: Provides limited bandwidth to Gray Zone communities at steep markup through reseller agreements with Gray Zone councils. The bandwidth is real. The 'limited' is adjustable based on political circumstances.
